name: Pantheon screenshot annotation tokens
sources: 2026 Pantheon Brand Guidelines, version 4.0 (Google Slides, pages 31-37 color, 41-43 typography, 70-77 diagrams). The 2023 guidelines and the 2025 presentation template, with Poppins, Aleo, and Purple, are deprecated.
Pantheon Message House for the AI Era and Pantheon Voice and Tone (October 2026) govern label wording; the Pantheon docs style guide governs docs. Neither sets a color or a font.

Color rules applied here: Ink and Paper carry the work; Yellow is rationed (one job at a time per surface) and never takes white type; Brick and Sky are reserved, one accent per artifact and never beside Yellow, so no annotation role uses them; hot pink is for live events only; the only permitted gradients are the four light motifs, so annotations use none.

Typography rules applied here: Inter for body, UI, and labels (Inter Tight is the display face and IBM Plex Serif Italic is the quote face; neither is used in annotations); sentence case everywhere except the uppercase label style.

Not in the guidelines: annotation colors for Do, Dont, and neutral notes. This contract carries Do and Dont by shape plus Ink and Paper, and drops the old Info blue, until the brand owners approve a color. See docs/reference/annotation-kit.md.

mark.note: Default mark and the main emphasis color. Ink and Paper carry the work; Yellow is spent once.

halo.note: Outline under Ink marks so they survive dark screenshot regions.

haloInk.note: Outline under Yellow and Paper marks. Yellow and Paper do not separate from a light screenshot on their own; an Ink halo does, and Yellow still reads against it on dark regions.

markYellow.note: The one focal step of a frame: its badge and its outline. Yellow is how the brand points; never more than one step per frame.

onYellow.note: Text on Yellow marks. Ink only; the brand never sets white type on Yellow.

ink.note: Low-emphasis notes, key caps, and the dim overlay.

paper.note: Neutral notes and the Dont mark: a Paper fill with an Ink halo.

do.note: Correct example. An Ink mark, always paired with a check marker.

dont.note: Mistaken example. A Paper mark with an Ink halo, always paired with a cross marker.

classify.note: Mean WCAG relative luminance of the clean screenshot under a mark. At or above the threshold is light; below is dark.

dark.note: Ink with its Paper halo reads on dark regions. Yellow, with its Ink halo, reads on both and is reserved for the one focal step.

marker.purpose: Numbered marker: identifies an ordered user action.

outline.purpose: Outline: identifies a control or region without obscuring it. Never filled.

highlight.purpose: Highlight: emphasizes a larger target area by dimming what surrounds it. Never placed over the target.

arrow.purpose: Arrow: connects explanatory text to a target.

label.purpose: Label: explains purpose or expected action.

marker.numeral: required, 1..N in reading order, no gaps or repeats
marker.sizes: S, M, L: diameters in metrics.badgePx

edgeRing.unit: px at the export scale, measured from the badge edge on the clean capture
edgeRing.note: A badge must not straddle a background edge (half on a dialog, half on the dimmed backdrop). The median luma (Rec. 601, 0-255) of opposite sides of the ring may differ by at most edgeLuma; pixels within skipDistance of the mark color are ignored.

outline.note: Solid marks the focus of the step; Dashed marks a secondary or optional area.
outline.nesting: Two outlines or highlights keep metrics.outlineGapPx of clear space between their outer edges (halo included). A mark nested inside another clears the outer mark's inner stroke edge by the same amount. A marker sits wholly inside a box or clear of its stroke.

highlight.note: Place over distracting regions only; it must not intersect any target.

arrow.head: The kit Arrow component's head (Head=End, or Both for ranges). It is not redrawn per run.

label.longText: Use Note box (Inter Regular body) for anything over four words.

pixelate.resample: Shrink the region with bilinear filtering, then enlarge it with nearest neighbor, so each block is one color averaged from the unredacted pixels under it.

redaction.note: Replace personal data with plausible fake data in the page before capture (preferred). Otherwise pixelate each declared region in the capture itself, before it goes to Figma, and keep the unredacted original out of anything delivered. Solid boxes and blur are not allowed: a box reads as a broken screenshot, and blur can be reversed.

typography.note: Inter is a free Google font and loads in every Figma file, so there is no fallback. Figma names the style "Semi Bold"; the brand guidelines write Semibold.

metrics.strokeRule: Strokes are authored for a 1440 px wide frame. At the docs display width a stroke must still render at 2 px or more, so on a wider frame the stroke scales up by frameWidth / displayWidth.

display.note: Rendered size is the authored size times min(1, docsColumnWidthPx / frameWidth).

contrast.note: WCAG 2.2 AA: 1.4.3 for text, 1.4.11 for marks. A mark is perceivable when its fill or its halo reaches 3:1 against the screenshot beneath it, and the fill reaches 3:1 against its halo.

logo.policy: Annotated screenshots carry no Pantheon logo. If one is genuinely needed, use an approved lockup with clear space and minimum size, and never recolor, stretch, rotate, distort, or cover it.

forbidden.note: No gradients as annotation label or component backgrounds.
